# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.
Начну с разведки: вытащу PR #30, его диф, комментарии ревью и состояние локального репозитория, чтобы понять, что там осталось недоделанным.

--- access.py ---
"""Access control helpers for MCP tools."""

from mcp_tracker.mcp.errors import TrackerError
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.errors import IssueNotFound


def _is_read_only_queue(settings: Settings, queue: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the given queue is configured as read-only."""
    return bool(
        settings.tracker_read_only_queues
        and queue.upper() in settings.tracker_read_only_queues
    )


def is_queue_allowed(settings: Settings, queue: str) -> bool:
    """Return True if the queue is reachable under ``TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES``.

    The raising `check_*_access` helpers below and the tools that filter whole
    listings share this one definition of the allow-list. Both settings hold a
    set of upper-cased keys (see `Settings.decode_queue_keys`), so the casing of
    the configuration does not matter and the check stays a hash lookup - which
    is what a listing tool does per row.
    """
    return (
        not settings.tracker_limit_queues
        or queue.upper() in settings.tracker_limit_queues
    )


def check_issue_access(
    settings: Settings, issue_id: str, *, write: bool = False
) -> None:
    """Check if access to the issue is allowed based on queue restrictions.

    When ``write`` is True, the target queue is additionally validated against
    the per-queue read-only allow-list (``TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES``); mutations
    on read-only queues are rejected.
    """
    queue = issue_id.split("-")[0]
    if not is_queue_allowed(settings, queue):
        raise IssueNotFound(issue_id)

def check_queue_access(
    settings: Settings, queue_id: str, *, write: bool = False
) -> None:
    """Check if access to the queue is allowed based on queue restrictions.

    When ``write`` is True, the queue is additionally validated against the
    per-queue read-only allow-list (``TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES``); mutations on
    read-only queues are rejected.
    """
    if not is_queue_allowed(settings, queue_id):
        raise TrackerError(f"Queue `{queue_id}` not found or not allowed.")
    if write and _is_read_only_queue(settings, queue_id):

"""Pagination helpers shared by the listing tools."""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Awaitable, Callable

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.pagination import ItemT, PaginatedResult


async def iter_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
) -> AsyncIterator[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]:
    """Yield the pages of a paginated Tracker listing.

    ``page`` returns that single page; None walks the listing from the first
    one. A walk stops as soon as the data is exhausted, which is either the
    page count Tracker reports or - when it reports none - a page shorter than
    ``per_page``.
    """
    current_page = 1 if page is None else page

    while True:
        batch = await fetch(current_page)
        if not batch.values:
            return

        yield batch

        if page is not None:
            return
        if batch.pages is not None:
            # Tracker says how many pages there are, so the walk can stop on the
            # last one instead of spending a request on the empty page past it.
            if current_page >= batch.pages:
                return
        elif len(batch.values) < per_page:
            return

        current_page += 1


async def collect_pages(
    fetch: Callable[[int], Awaitable[PaginatedResult[ItemT]]],
    *,
    page: int | None,
    per_page: int,
    visible: Callable[[list[ItemT]], list[ItemT]] | None = None,
    restricted: bool = False,
) -> PaginatedResult[ItemT]:
    """Collect ``page`` alone, or every page, into one result.

    ``visible`` filters each batch down to what the caller may see. Doing so
    makes the totals Tracker reported describe more than ``values`` holds, so
    they are dropped whenever ``restricted`` says a filter is configured - as
    they are on a full walk, which already returned every item there is.
    Keeping that decision here is what stops a new listing tool from reporting
    totals that count the rows it just hid.
    """
    values: list[ItemT] = []
    last_page: PaginatedResult[ItemT] | None = None

    async for batch in iter_pages(fetch, page=page, per_page=per_page):
        last_page = batch
        values.extend(visible(batch.values) if visible else batch.values)

    if last_page is None or restricted or page is None:
        return PaginatedResult[ItemT](values=values)

    return PaginatedResult[ItemT](
        values=values, hits=last_page.hits, pages=last_page.pages
    )

"""Read-only probe of the component endpoints on the live Tracker org.

Only GET requests. Prints status, the pagination headers and a trimmed body,
never the token.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys

from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.client import ServiceAccountSettings, TrackerClient

PROBES = [
    ("GET", "v3/components", {"perPage": 2, "page": 1}),
    ("GET", "v3/components", {"perPage": 2, "page": 2}),
    ("GET", "v3/components", {"queue": "FLATICA"}),
    ("GET", "v3/queues/FLATICA/components", None),
    ("GET", "v3/components/856", None),
    ("GET", "v3/components/999999999", None),
]


def trim(body: bytes, limit: int = 900) -> str:
    text = body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except ValueError:
        return text[:limit]
    if isinstance(data, list):
        summary = {"count": len(data), "first": data[:2]}
        return json.dumps(summary, ensure_ascii=False)[:limit]
    return json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)[:limit]


async def main() -> None:
    settings = Settings()
    if not (settings.tracker_token or settings.tracker_iam_token or settings.tracker_sa_key_id):
        print("no credentials in the environment; nothing probed")
        sys.exit(1)

    service_account = None
    if settings.tracker_sa_key_id and settings.tracker_sa_service_account_id and settings.tracker_sa_private_key:
        service_account = ServiceAccountSettings(
            key_id=settings.tracker_sa_key_id,
            service_account_id=settings.tracker_sa_service_account_id,
            private_key=settings.tracker_sa_private_key,
        )

    client = TrackerClient(
        base_url=settings.tracker_api_base_url,
        token=settings.tracker_token,
        token_type=settings.oauth_token_type,
        iam_token=settings.tracker_iam_token,
        service_account=service_account,
        cloud_org_id=settings.tracker_cloud_org_id,
        org_id=settings.tracker_org_id,
        timeout=settings.tracker_api_timeout,
    )
    await client.prepare()
    try:
        for method, url, params in PROBES:
            print(f"\n=== {method} {url} params={params}")
            headers = await client._build_headers(None)
            async with client._session.request(method, url, headers=headers, params=params) as response:
                body = await response.read()
                interesting = {
                    k: v
                    for k, v in response.headers.items()
                    if k.lower().startswith("x-total") or k.lower() in {"link", "content-type"}
                }
                print("status:", response.status, "headers:", interesting)
                print("body:", trim(body))
    finally:
        await client.close()


asyncio.run(main())

Разведка закончена, ниже состояние PR и вопросы, без ответов на которые дальше идти не хочу.

**Что с PR #30 сейчас.** Голова ветки `component-management` в форке asanisimov (6 коммитов, база от 0.7.x). С `main` конфликтует во всех 10 общих файлах: с тех пор появились `_request()`-воронка, `collect_pages`/`PaginatedResult`, `check_queue_access(write=True)` для `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES`, протоколы boards/templates/entities и правила в `rules/` с тестами на имена, длину описаний и покрытие README. Ребейз тут равен переписыванию, так что план: новая ветка от `main`, перенос руками.

**Из твоего ревью закрыто:** файлы докоммичены, `lead`/`assign_auto` на create, split read/write, баг кеша `component_get`, обход `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` (через `check_component_access`), `components_get_all`, `Component.queue`, тесты разнесены по файлам, isort.

**Осталось открытым (твой ревью от 20 июля):**
- `assign_auto` в `component_update` так и не добавлен.
- `version` не принимается от агента: клиент всегда делает GET перед PATCH, оптимистичная блокировка не работает.
- В модели `Component` нет `lead` и `assignAuto`, только `queue`.
- `destructiveHint` на delete нет.
- update/delete делают GET ради проверки доступа даже когда ограничений не настроено.
- Нет упоминания компонентов в инструкциях сервера, README, CHANGELOG.
- Плюс новое с `main`: `write=True` для read-only очередей, `_request()` вместо прямых `self._session`, `ComponentNotFound` на 404, `component` в `TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES`, описания в бюджете 40-350 символов, manifest.

**Проверил на живой организации (только GET, ничего не менял):**

| Эндпоинт | Результат |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v3/queues/{key}?expand=components` | только ссылки `{id: "856", display: "Design"}`, без версии, lead и assignAuto |
| `GET /v3/components` (документирован) | вся организация, 1002 компонента, 501 страница по 2; параметр `queue=` игнорируется |
| `GET /v3/queues/{key}/components` (не документирован) | полные объекты только этой очереди, без пагинации |
| `GET /v3/components/{id}` (не документирован) | полный объект; на несуществующий id 404 «Компонент не существует.» |

То есть `components_get_all` из PR с фильтром по очереди на этой организации сделает 21 запрос ради 13 компонентов. А `queue_get_metadata` с `expand=components` даёт ровно то, что нужно `issue_create` (id и имя), но не версию для update. Пересечение с новым тулом реальное, но данные разные.

"""Verify the undocumented component write endpoints on the live org.

Creates ONE throwaway component in the queue given as argv[1], patches it,
patches it again with a stale version, deletes it, and reads it back. The
delete runs in `finally`, so the component does not outlive the script.
Prints statuses, headers of interest and bodies; never the token.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys

from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.client import TrackerClient

QUEUE = sys.argv[1]
NAME = "mcp-test-2026-09-06"


def show(label: str, status: int, body: bytes) -> dict | list | None:
    text = body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text) if text else None
    except ValueError:
        data = None
    print(f"--- {label}: status {status}")
    print("   ", (json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False) if data is not None else repr(text))[:1200])
    return data


async def call(client: TrackerClient, method: str, url: str, **kwargs):
    headers = await client._build_headers(None)
    async with client._session.request(method, url, headers=headers, **kwargs) as response:
        return response.status, await response.read()


async def main() -> None:
    settings = Settings()
    client = TrackerClient(
        base_url=settings.tracker_api_base_url,
        token=settings.tracker_token,
        token_type=settings.oauth_token_type,
        iam_token=settings.tracker_iam_token,
        service_account=None,

    @staticmethod
    async def _raise_for_status(response: ClientResponse) -> None:
        """Raise `TrackerAPIError` carrying the API's own explanation of the failure.

        `ClientResponse.raise_for_status()` discards the response body, which is
        where Tracker says *what* it did not like (e.g. which field of an
        issue_create call was rejected with 422), leaving the caller with a bare
        "Unprocessable Entity".
        """
        if response.status < 400:
            return

        try:
            body = await response.text()
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - body already consumed/aborted
            body = ""

        raise TrackerAPIError(
            status=response.status,
            method=response.method,
            url=str(response.url),
            body=body,
        )

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def _request(
        self,
        method: str,
        url: str,
        *,
        auth: YandexAuth | None,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        json: Any = None,
        not_found: YandexTrackerError | None = None,
        conflict: YandexTrackerError | None = None,
        allow_statuses: Collection[int] = (),
    ) -> AsyncIterator[ClientResponse]:
        """Every request to the Tracker API goes through here.

        What is handled once here used to be repeated at each of the sixty call
        sites, which is one forgotten line away from a method that reports a
        failure worse than the rest: the timeout below reached the caller from a
        single method until this existed, and a missing `not_found` turns "no
        such issue" back into a bare 404.

        `allow_statuses` hands a status back to the caller instead of raising -
        for the one method that answers a 404 with `None` rather than an error.
        """
        # Built before the `try`: the service account's IAM fetch is not a
        # Tracker request and must not be reported as one timing out.
        headers = await self._build_headers(auth)

        try:
            async with self._session.request(
                method, url, headers=headers, params=params, json=json
            ) as response:
                if response.status not in allow_statuses:
                    if not_found is not None and response.status == 404:
                        raise not_found
                    if conflict is not None and response.status == 409:
                        raise conflict
                    await self._raise_for_status(response)
                yield response
        except TimeoutError as exc:
            # A body read that times out lands here too: it runs inside the
            # caller's `async with`, and that exception is thrown back in at the
            # `yield` above.
            raise TrackerAPITimeout(
                method=method, url=url, timeout=self._timeout
            ) from exc

class TrackerAPIError(YandexTrackerError):
    """A non-2xx response from the Yandex Tracker API.

    Tracker explains *why* a request was rejected in the response body
    (`errorMessages` / `errors`), which is the only way to tell, for example,
    which field of an issue_create call was invalid. The body is therefore part
    of the raised error instead of being dropped by `raise_for_status()`.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, status: int, method: str, url: str, body: str):
        self.status = status
        self.method = method
        self.url = url
        self.body = body
        self.error_messages, self.errors = _parse_error_body(body)

        details: list[str] = list(self.error_messages)
        details.extend(f"{field}: {message}" for field, message in self.errors.items())
        if not details and body:
            details.append(body[:MAX_ERROR_BODY_LENGTH])

        message = f"Yandex Tracker API error {status} on {method} {url}"
        if details:
            message += ": " + "; ".join(details)
        super().__init__(message)


def _parse_error_body(body: str) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, str]]:
    """Extract Tracker's `errorMessages` / `errors` from an error response body."""
    try:
        parsed: Any = json.loads(body)
    except ValueError:
        return [], {}

    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
        return [], {}

    raw_messages = parsed.get("errorMessages")
    messages = [str(m) for m in raw_messages] if isinstance(raw_messages, list) else []

    raw_errors = parsed.get("errors")
    errors = (
        {str(k): str(v) for k, v in raw_errors.items()}
        if isinstance(raw_errors, dict)
        else {}
    )

    return messages, errors

"""Guard: entity models must speak Tracker's own field names on the wire."""

import importlib
import inspect
import pkgutil

import pytest
from pydantic import BaseModel

import mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types as types_package
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.issues import resolve_issue_field


def _aliased_fields() -> list[tuple[str, str, list[str], str | None]]:
    """Collect (model, field, validation aliases, serialization alias) triples."""
    collected: list[tuple[str, str, list[str], str | None]] = []
    for module_info in pkgutil.iter_modules(types_package.__path__):
        module = importlib.import_module(f"{types_package.__name__}.{module_info.name}")
        for obj in vars(module).values():
            if (
                not inspect.isclass(obj)
                or not issubclass(obj, BaseModel)
                or obj.__module__ != module.__name__
            ):
                continue
            for field_name, field in obj.model_fields.items():
                aliases = getattr(field.validation_alias, "choices", None)
                if aliases is None:
                    continue
                collected.append(
                    (obj.__name__, field_name, list(aliases), field.serialization_alias)
                )
    return collected


ALIASED_FIELDS = _aliased_fields()


class TestModelAliases:
    def test_models_declare_aliases(self) -> None:
        assert ALIASED_FIELDS, (
            "no aliased fields discovered - the sweep below is vacuous"
        )

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("model", "field", "aliases", "serialization_alias"),
        ALIASED_FIELDS,
        ids=[f"{model}.{field}" for model, field, _, _ in ALIASED_FIELDS],
    )
    def test_serializes_under_the_tracker_name(
        self,
        model: str,
        field: str,
        aliases: list[str],
        serialization_alias: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        """A field that accepts Tracker's name must also emit it.

        Otherwise a response can not be fed back into a write call: the reader

        assert serialization_alias == wire_name, (
            f"{model}.{field} accepts '{wire_name}' but serializes as "
            f"'{serialization_alias or field}'"

# Queue components: implementation spec

Branch `feat/queue-components` (checked out, clean, forked from `main` at 0c9a415).
This finishes PR https://github.com/aikts/yandex-tracker-mcp/pull/30 by asanisimov,
re-implemented on top of the current `main`. Read `AGENTS.md` and every file in
`rules/` first: names, description budgets, README tables, CHANGELOG shape and the
tests that enforce them are all rules here, not suggestions.

The PR's own code is reachable as `origin/pr/30` (`git diff f2764b0 origin/pr/30`) -
use it as a source of test ideas and payload shapes, not as something to cherry-pick:
it predates the `_request()` funnel, `check_queue_access(write=True)`,
`collect_pages` and the `rules/` tests.

## Decisions already made (do not reopen)

- Read side: `queue_get_components(queue_id)` on `GET v3/queues/{queue}/components`,
  plus `component_get(component_id)` on `GET v3/components/{id}`. The PR's
  org-wide `components_get_all` is dropped. `queue_get_metadata` and its
  `expand=components` option are left exactly as they are.
- Write side: `component_create`, `component_update`, `component_delete` - a new
  entity `component`, added to `TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES` in
  `tests/mcp/server/test_tool_conventions.py` and to the entity list in
  `rules/tool-naming.md`.
- Commits are ours; asanisimov is credited with a
  `Co-authored-by: Alexandr Anisimov <asanisimovq@yandex.ru>` trailer. Do NOT
  commit - the human does that after review.

## Verified against the live Tracker API on 2026-09-06 (record these in AGENTS.md)

Read (GET only, org with 1002 components across ~400 queues):

- `GET v3/queues/{key}?expand=components` returns only references:
  `{"self": ..., "id": "856", "display": "Design"}` - id as a string, no version,
  lead, description or assignAuto. Absent key when the queue has none (the
  existing `queue_get_metadata` already turns that into `[]`).
- `GET v3/components` (the only documented read) is org-wide: `perPage`/`page` work,
  `X-Total-Count: 1002`, `X-Total-Pages: 501` at perPage=2; a `queue=` query
  parameter is ignored. Not used by this feature - listing a queue's 13 components
  this way costs 21 requests.
- `GET v3/queues/{key}/components` (undocumented) answers 200 with the full
  component objects of that queue only, no pagination headers:
  `{"self","id": 856,"version": 1,"name","queue": {self,id,key,display},
  "lead": {self,id,display,cloudUid,passportUid?},"assignAuto": false}` -
  `description` and `lead` are absent when unset.
- `GET v3/components/{id}` (undocumented) answers 200 with the same full object;
  an unknown id answers 404 `{"errorMessages": ["Компонент не существует."]}`.

Write (one throwaway component in queue AP, id 1061, created and deleted):

- `POST v3/components` with `{"queue": "AP", "name": ..., "description": ...}`
  answers 201 with the full object, `version: 1`. `lead` is a login string
  (documented), `assignAuto` a boolean.
- `PATCH v3/components/{id}?version=1` with `{"description": ..., "assignAuto": true}`
  answers 200, `version: 2`.
- `PATCH` with a stale `version` answers **412** (not 409):
  `{"errorMessages": ["Компонент: не удалось сохранить изменения, попробуйте ещё раз."]}`.
- `PATCH` without `version` answers **428**:
  `"Необходимо указать либо параметр 'версия', либо значение заголовка If-Match."` -
  so the client method must always send it.
- `PATCH` with `{"lead": "<login>"}` answers 200 and returns `lead` as a user object.
- `PATCH` with an empty body `{}` answers 200 and changes nothing (version stays).
- `DELETE v3/components/{id}` (undocumented) answers 204 with no body and takes no
  `version`. Deleting again, or reading after deleting, answers the 404 above.

## Layers to build

### Types - `mcp_tracker/tracker/proto/types/components.py`

```python
class Component(BaseTrackerEntity):
    id: int
    version: int
    name: str
    description: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    queue: QueueReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    lead: UserReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    assign_auto: bool | None = Field(
        None,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("assignAuto", "assign_auto"),
        serialization_alias="assignAuto",
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
    )
```

`QueueReference` / `UserReference` are in `types/refs.py`. The alias pair is what
`tests/tracker/proto/test_model_aliases.py` checks. Required `id`/`version`/`name`
mirror `QueueVersion`, the closest sibling; test fixtures use `model_construct()`.

### Errors - `mcp_tracker/tracker/custom/errors.py`

- `ComponentNotFound(component_id: int)` - "Component with ID '{id}' not found."
- `ComponentVersionConflict(component_id: int, version: int)` - an editing
  conflict: the component was changed since that version was read; re-read it with
  `component_get` (or `queue_get_components`) and retry, or omit `version` on
  `component_update` to update the current one. Do not copy the issue wording about
  triggers and automation - nothing bumps a component's version behind your back.
- `ComponentEmptyUpdate()` - a `component_update` that passes none of `name`,
  `description`, `lead`, `assign_auto` is refused locally (the API answers 200 and
  does nothing), like `ChecklistItemEmptyUpdate`.

### Request funnel - `mcp_tracker/tracker/custom/client.py`

`_request()` raises `conflict` on 409 only. Extend it to `(409, 412)`: 412 is
Tracker's answer to a stale component `version`, and a 412 anywhere else is the same
kind of precondition failure. Update the docstring, add a case to
`tests/tracker/custom/test_request.py`, and update the *Errors* bullet under
*Talking to the Tracker API* in AGENTS.md.

### Protocols

- `QueuesProtocol.queues_get_components(queue_id, *, auth) -> list[Component]` next
  to `queues_get_versions`. Client: `GET v3/queues/{queue_id}/components`,
  `not_found=QueueNotFound(queue_id)`, via `self._read()`. Caching wrapper with
  `@cached`.
- New `mcp_tracker/tracker/proto/components.py`: `ComponentsProtocol` +
  `ComponentsProtocolWrap` (copy the shape of `proto/boards.py`):
  - `component_get(component_id: int, *, auth) -> Component` -
    `GET v3/components/{id}`, `not_found=ComponentNotFound(component_id)`. Cached.
  - `component_create(queue_id: str, *, name: str, description: str | None = None,
    lead: str | None = None, assign_auto: bool | None = None, auth) -> Component` -
    `POST v3/components`, body `{"queue": queue_id, "name": name}` plus the optional
    ones only when not None (`assignAuto` on the wire).
  - `component_update(component_id: int, *, version: int, name=None,
    description=None, lead=None, assign_auto=None, auth) -> Component` -
    `PATCH v3/components/{id}` with `params={"version": version}`; raise
    `ComponentEmptyUpdate` before any request when the body would be empty;
    `not_found=ComponentNotFound(...)`, `conflict=ComponentVersionConflict(...)`.
    `version` is required here on purpose (the API answers 428 without it); the
    tool is what fills it in.
  - `component_delete(component_id: int, *, auth) -> None` -
    `DELETE v3/components/{id}`, `not_found=ComponentNotFound(...)`, no version.
  - Docstrings say which endpoints are undocumented and that they were verified on
    2026-09-06 (the way `issue_update_checklist_item` documents its quirks).
- `TrackerClient` inherits `ComponentsProtocol` too; `AppContext.components`;
  `CacheCollection.components`; `CachingComponentsProtocol` in
  `caching/client.py` overriding **every** protocol method (the PR's first version
  forgot `component_get`, which then returned `None` under `TOOLS_CACHE_ENABLED`);
  wiring in `make_tracker_lifespan` in `mcp/server.py`.

### Access - `mcp_tracker/mcp/tools/_access.py`

- `queue_checks_needed(settings, *, write: bool) -> bool`: True when
  `tracker_limit_queues` is set, or when `write` and `tracker_read_only_queues` is
  set. This is what lets update/delete skip the extra GET on an unrestricted server
  (review comment by igorcoding, 2026-07-20).
- `check_component_access(settings, component, *, write=False)`: no-op unless
  `queue_checks_needed`; then a component without a `queue.key` is refused with
  `TrackerError` (its queue cannot be checked), otherwise
  `check_queue_access(settings, component.queue.key, write=write)`.
- Unit tests in `tests/mcp/tools/test_access.py`.

### Tools

Names, modules and registration:

- `queue_get_components` in `mcp/tools/queue.py` (registered with the queue tools).
- `component_get` in new `mcp/tools/component.py`, `register_component_tools`.
- `component_create` / `component_update` / `component_delete` in new
  `mcp/tools/component_write.py`, `register_component_write_tools`, registered only
  when `not settings.tracker_read_only`. Update `mcp/tools/__init__.py` (docstring
  and both registration blocks).

Shared parameters go to `mcp/params.py` as `Annotated` aliases (rule: never paste a
`Field(description=...)` between two tools): `ComponentID` (numeric id, from
`queue_get_components` or an issue's `components` field), `ComponentNameParam`,
`ComponentDescriptionParam`, `ComponentLeadParam` (a user **login**, e.g.
`i.ivanov`, not a display name or uid), `ComponentAssignAutoParam` (new issues with
this component get the lead as assignee), `ComponentVersionParam`. Create and update
use the same aliases; on update `name` is optional.

Behaviour:

- `queue_get_components(queue_id)`: `check_queue_access(settings, queue_id)`, then
  `queues.queues_get_components`. Returns `list[Component]`.
- `component_get(component_id)`: `components.component_get`, then
  `check_component_access(settings, component)`. Returns `Component`.
- `component_create(queue_id, name, description=None, lead=None, assign_auto=None)`:
  `check_queue_access(settings, queue_id, write=True)`, then create. Returns
  `Component`.
- `component_update(component_id, name=None, description=None, lead=None,
  assign_auto=None, version=None)`: when `version is None` or
  `queue_checks_needed(settings, write=True)`, read the component once with
  `component_get`, run `check_component_access(..., write=True)`, and take the
  version from it if the caller gave none. Exactly one GET at most, then one PATCH.
  Returns `Component`.
- `component_delete(component_id)`: when `queue_checks_needed(settings, write=True)`,
  read once and `check_component_access(..., write=True)`; otherwise go straight to
  the DELETE. Returns `None` (check how the other `*_delete` tools in this repo
  return nothing and match). `ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=True)`.

Descriptions, per `rules/tool-descriptions.md` (40-350 characters, first sentence
carries the entity noun and the Russian term 'компоненты' / 'компонент', a second
sentence only for a trap):

- `queue_get_components`: the queue's components with lead, auto-assign flag and
  `version`; `queue_get_metadata` with expand=['components'] names them only (id and
  name), and the id is what `issue_create` / `issue_update` take in `components`.
- `component_get`: one component by numeric id, with `queue`, `lead`, `assignAuto`
  and the `version` `component_update` takes; ids come from `queue_get_components`
  or an issue's `components`.
- `component_create`: create a component in a queue - a label grouping the queue's
  issues by product, process or owner; `lead` is a login.
- `component_update`: change name, description, lead or auto-assign; omitted fields
  keep their value; `version` is optional and, when given, rejects the update if the
  component changed since.
- `component_delete`: permanently delete a component; cannot be undone.

Also touch:

- `_COMPONENTS_DESCRIPTION` in `mcp/params.py` and the `id` description of
  `IssueComponentRef` in `proto/types/inputs.py`: name `queue_get_components` as the
  source of ids (keep `queue_get_metadata` with expand as the other one). Keep them
  short.
- Server instructions in `mcp/params.py`: add a "Use these tools to" line for reading
  and managing queue components with the one-line definition ("group a queue's issues
  by product, process or owner"), and `components - "компоненты"` to the Russian
  terms line. `tests/mcp/server/test_instructions.py` fails on a backticked name that
  is neither a tool nor in `NON_TOOL_NAMES` - add to that set if you backtick a
  non-tool.

### Tests (pytest, asyncio auto, aioresponses, AsyncMock(spec=...), parametrize over loops)

- `tests/mcp/conftest.py`: `mock_components_protocol` (`AsyncMock(spec=ComponentsProtocol)`),
  passed into `mock_app_context`.
- `tests/mcp/tools/conftest.py`: `sample_component` (`Component.model_construct`, with
  `queue=QueueReference(key="TEST", ...)`, `lead=UserReference(...)`, `version=1`),
  `sample_components`.
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_queue_tools.py`: `TestQueueGetComponents` - success, protocol
  args, restricted queue with `client_session_with_limits`.
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_component_tools.py` (`component_get`): success; registered in
  `client_session_read_only`; with `client_session_with_limits` a component whose
  queue is `RESTRICTED` is rejected after the GET, one whose queue is `ALLOWED` passes.
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_component_write_tools.py`: for each of create/update/delete -
  success and `call_args`, optional parameters provided vs omitted (`lead`,
  `assign_auto`, `description`, `version`), not registered under
  `client_session_read_only`, `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` (`client_session_with_limits`)
  and `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES` (`client_session_with_read_only_queues`) rejections,
  and the round-trip accounting: on an unrestricted server `component_update` with
  `version` given makes **no** `component_get` call, without `version` exactly one;
  `component_delete` makes no `component_get` call unrestricted and exactly one under
  limits. `component_update` with nothing to change is an error and reaches no
  protocol call... (the check lives in the client, so at the tool level assert the
  client mock is called with the arguments as given; the empty-update test belongs to
  the client tests).
- `tests/tracker/custom/queues/test_queues_get_components.py` and
  `tests/tracker/custom/components/test_component_{get,create,update,delete}.py`:
  URL, method, headers (`RequestCapture` from `tests/aioresponses_utils.py`),
  query `version` on PATCH, body contents (`assignAuto` spelling, optional fields
  omitted when None), response parsing (`lead`, `assign_auto`, `queue`), 404 →
  `ComponentNotFound` / `QueueNotFound`, 412 → `ComponentVersionConflict`, empty
  update → `ComponentEmptyUpdate` with no request made, 204 on delete. Use the live
  payload shapes above.
- `tests/tracker/caching/test_components_protocol.py` (every method delegates to
  `_original`, with and without auth), add `queues_get_components` to
  `test_queues_protocol.py`, and a case in `test_protocol_conformance.py`.
- `tests/tracker/custom/test_request.py`: 412 raises the `conflict` error.
- `tests/mcp/tools/test_access.py`: `queue_checks_needed` and `check_component_access`.
- `tests/mcp/server/test_server_creation.py`: `queue_get_components`, `component_get`
  → `READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`; `component_create/update/delete` → `WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`
  (and the counts in the comments).
- `tests/mcp/server/test_tool_conventions.py`: `"component"` in `TOOL_NAME_ENTITIES`.

### Docs

- `manifest.json`: one sentence per tool, under 160 characters, for the five tools.
- `README.md` and `README_ru.md` (same sections, same order, same anchors): a
  `queue_get_components` row in the Queues table, and a new `<details>` section
  "Components" / "Компоненты" right after Queues with the four `component_*` rows and
  at most three bullets under the table: the allow-lists apply through the
  component's queue (and update/delete read the component to learn it); `version` on
  `component_update` is optional; `component_delete` is permanent. Also mention the
  read side once: `queue_get_metadata` gives ids and names, `queue_get_components`
  the full objects.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under `## [Unreleased]` → `### Features`: one bold-led bullet for the
  component tools, linking the PR (#30) - the shape and size in `rules/changelog.md`.
- `AGENTS.md`: the protocol list (`ComponentsProtocol`, `components` on
  `AppContext`), the MCP tools module list, the tool categories table (Component /
  Component Write), and a new bullet under *Talking to the Tracker API* with the
  verified facts above (which endpoints are undocumented, 412/428, empty PATCH is a
  no-op, DELETE takes no version, `expand=components` returns references only).
- `rules/tool-naming.md`: add `component` to the entity list.

## Definition of done

`task` (format, lint, type check, tests) passes. Report what you changed, anything
in this spec you could not follow and why, and any behaviour you had to guess.

from typing import Any

from mcp.server import FastMCP
from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context
from mcp.types import ToolAnnotations

from mcp_tracker.mcp.context import AppContext
from mcp_tracker.mcp.params import (
    ComponentAssignAutoParam,
    ComponentDescriptionParam,
    ComponentID,
    ComponentLeadParam,
    ComponentNameOptionalParam,
    ComponentNameParam,
    ComponentVersionParam,
    QueueID,
)
from mcp_tracker.mcp.tools._access import (
    check_component_access,
    check_queue_access,
    queue_checks_needed,
)
from mcp_tracker.mcp.utils import get_yandex_auth
from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.components import Component


def register_component_write_tools(settings: Settings, mcp: FastMCP[Any]) -> None:
    """Register queue component write tools (not registered in read-only mode)."""

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Create Component",
        description="Create a component (in russian - 'компонент') in a Yandex "
        "Tracker queue - a label grouping the queue's issues by product, process or "
        "owner; `lead` is a user login.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=False),
    )
    async def component_create(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        queue_id: QueueID,
        name: ComponentNameParam,
        description: ComponentDescriptionParam = None,
        lead: ComponentLeadParam = None,
        assign_auto: ComponentAssignAutoParam = None,
    ) -> Component:
        check_queue_access(settings, queue_id, write=True)
        return await ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.components.component_create(
            queue_id,
            name=name,
            description=description,
            lead=lead,
            assign_auto=assign_auto,
            auth=get_yandex_auth(ctx),
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Update Component",
        description="Change the name, description, lead or auto-assign flag of a "
        "Yandex Tracker queue component (in russian - 'компонент'); omitted fields "
        "keep their value. `version` is optional and, when given, rejects the update "
        "if the component changed since it was read.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=False),
    )
    async def component_update(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        component_id: ComponentID,
        name: ComponentNameOptionalParam = None,
        description: ComponentDescriptionParam = None,
        lead: ComponentLeadParam = None,
        assign_auto: ComponentAssignAutoParam = None,
        version: ComponentVersionParam = None,
    ) -> Component:
        components = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.components
        auth = get_yandex_auth(ctx)

        # One read at most: the API needs a version (428 without one), and a
        # restricted server needs the queue to check. Both come from the same
        # GET, which is skipped when the caller supplied the version and the
        # server has nothing to check.
        if version is None or queue_checks_needed(settings, write=True):
            component = await components.component_get(component_id, auth=auth)
            check_component_access(settings, component, write=True)
            if version is None:
                version = component.version

        return await components.component_update(
            component_id,
            version=version,
            name=name,
            description=description,
            lead=lead,
            assign_auto=assign_auto,
            auth=auth,
        )

    @mcp.tool(
        title="Delete Component",
        description="Permanently delete a Yandex Tracker queue component (in russian "
        "- 'компонент') by its numeric id. This cannot be undone.",
        annotations=ToolAnnotations(readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=True),
    )
    async def component_delete(
        ctx: Context[Any, AppContext],
        component_id: ComponentID,
    ) -> None:
        components = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context.components
        auth = get_yandex_auth(ctx)

        # The argument names no queue: read the component to learn it, but
        # only when there is a restriction to check it against.
        if queue_checks_needed(settings, write=True):
            component = await components.component_get(component_id, auth=auth)
            check_component_access(settings, component, write=True)

        await components.component_delete(component_id, auth=auth)

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

from .common import YandexAuth
from .types.components import Component


@runtime_checkable
class ComponentsProtocol(Protocol):
    async def component_get(
        self, component_id: int, *, auth: YandexAuth | None = None
    ) -> Component: ...

    async def component_create(
        self,
        queue_id: str,
        *,
        name: str,
        description: str | None = None,
        lead: str | None = None,
        assign_auto: bool | None = None,
        auth: YandexAuth | None = None,
    ) -> Component: ...

    async def component_update(
        self,
        component_id: int,
        *,
        version: int,
        name: str | None = None,
        description: str | None = None,
        lead: str | None = None,
        assign_auto: bool | None = None,
        auth: YandexAuth | None = None,
    ) -> Component: ...

    async def component_delete(
        self, component_id: int, *, auth: YandexAuth | None = None
    ) -> None: ...


class ComponentsProtocolWrap(ComponentsProtocol):
    def __init__(self, original: ComponentsProtocol):
        self._original = original

from pydantic import AliasChoices, Field

from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.base import (
    BaseTrackerEntity,
    NoneExcludedField,
    none_excluder,
)
from mcp_tracker.tracker.proto.types.refs import QueueReference, UserReference


class Component(BaseTrackerEntity):
    """A queue component, as `GET /v3/queues/{queue}/components` and
    `GET /v3/components/{id}` return it.

    `description` and `lead` are absent from the response when unset, which
    the `NoneExcludedField` defaults mirror. `version` is what
    `component_update` has to send (the API answers 428 without it).
    """

    id: int
    version: int
    name: str
    description: str | None = NoneExcludedField
    queue: QueueReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    lead: UserReference | None = NoneExcludedField
    assign_auto: bool | None = Field(
        None,
        validation_alias=AliasChoices("assignAuto", "assign_auto"),
        serialization_alias="assignAuto",
        exclude_if=none_excluder,
    )

"""Second live probe: what `lead` accepts on PATCH, and what clears it.

One throwaway component in the queue given as argv[1]; deleted in `finally`.
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys

from mcp_tracker.settings import Settings
from mcp_tracker.tracker.custom.client import TrackerClient

QUEUE = sys.argv[1]
NAME = "mcp-test-2026-09-06-lead"


def show(label: str, status: int, body: bytes):
    text = body.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text) if text else None
    except ValueError:
        data = None
    lead = data.get("lead") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    print(f"--- {label}: status {status}; version={data.get('version') if isinstance(data, dict) else None}; "
          f"lead={json.dumps(lead, ensure_ascii=False) if lead else lead}; "
          f"description={data.get('description') if isinstance(data, dict) else None!r}")
    if status >= 400:
        print("    ", (json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False) if data is not None else repr(text))[:400])
    return data


async def call(client: TrackerClient, method: str, url: str, **kwargs):
    headers = await client._build_headers(None)
    async with client._session.request(method, url, headers=headers, **kwargs) as response:
        return response.status, await response.read()


async def main() -> None:
    settings = Settings()
    client = TrackerClient(
        base_url=settings.tracker_api_base_url,
        token=settings.tracker_token,
        token_type=settings.oauth_token_type,
        iam_token=settings.tracker_iam_token,
        service_account=None,
        cloud_org_id=settings.tracker_cloud_org_id,
        org_id=settings.tracker_org_id,
        timeout=settings.tracker_api_timeout,
    )
    await client.prepare()
    component_id = None
    try:
        status, body = await call(client, "GET", "v3/myself")
        me = json.loads(body)
        login, uid = me["login"], me["uid"]
        print("me:", login, uid)

        status, body = await call(
            client, "POST", "v3/components",
            json={"queue": QUEUE, "name": NAME, "description": "probe", "lead": login},
        )
        created = show("create with lead=login", status, body)
        if status not in (200, 201):
            return
        component_id = created["id"]
        version = created["version"]

        async def patch(label: str, payload):
            nonlocal version
            status, body = await call(
                client, "PATCH", f"v3/components/{component_id}",
                params={"version": version}, json=payload,
            )
            data = show(label, status, body)
            if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("version"):
                version = data["version"]
            return data

        await patch("lead = uid as int", {"lead": uid})
        await patch("lead = uid as string", {"lead": str(uid)})
        await patch("lead = {id: uid}", {"lead": {"id": str(uid)}})
        await patch("lead = null", {"lead": None})
        await patch("lead = ''", {"lead": ""})
        await patch("lead = {}", {"lead": {}})
        await patch("lead = login again", {"lead": login})
        await patch("lead = 'no-such-login-xyz'", {"lead": "no-such-login-xyz"})
        await patch("description = ''", {"description": ""})
        await patch("description = null", {"description": None})
        await patch("name = ''", {"name": ""})
        status, body = await call(client, "GET", f"v3/components/{component_id}")
        show("final read", status, body)
    finally:
        if component_id is not None:
            status, body = await call(client, "DELETE", f"v3/components/{component_id}")
            print("delete:", status)
        await client.close()


asyncio.run(main())

**Что в ветке (41 файл, +2406 строк).** Пять тулов: `queue_get_components`, `component_get`, `component_create`, `component_update`, `component_delete`. Слои по чеклисту AGENTS.md: модель `Component`, `ComponentsProtocol` плюс `queues_get_components` в `QueuesProtocol`, клиент через `_read()`, кеш-обёртка, `AppContext`, тулы, ошибки `ComponentNotFound` / `ComponentVersionConflict` / `ComponentEmptyUpdate` / `ComponentClearConflict`, тесты всех слоёв, manifest, оба README (новая секция «Components» после очередей), CHANGELOG, AGENTS.md, `rules/tool-naming.md`. Все замечания из твоего ревью PR #30 закрыты, включая незакрытые на июль: `assign_auto` на update, `version` от агента, поля `lead` / `assignAuto` в модели, `destructiveHint`, GET только при необходимости, инструкции сервера.

**Проверено на живой организации** (два временных компонента в AP, оба удалены):

| Факт | Следствие в коде |
| --- | --- |
| PATCH без `version` → 428, с устаревшей → 412 | `version` обязателен в клиенте, тул читает компонент, если агент его не передал; `_request()` теперь маппит 412 на `conflict=` рядом с 409 |
| Пустое тело PATCH → 200 без изменений | локальный отказ `ComponentEmptyUpdate` |
| `lead: {}` очищает, `null` игнорируется, `""` → 422 | `clear_lead` на `component_update` по образцу `clear_assignee` |
| `lead` принимает логин, uid числом и строкой | описание параметра говорит «login or uid» |
| DELETE без версии → 204, повторный → 404 | `component_delete` без `version`, 404 → `ComponentNotFound` |
| `GET /v3/queues/{key}/components` отдаёт полные объекты одной очереди | на нём построен `queue_get_components` |

**Решения, которые принял сам, можно отменить:**
- Чтения компонентов не кешируются под `TOOLS_CACHE_ENABLED`: их `version` нужен для PATCH, кешированное чтение после записи давало бы 412 до конца TTL.
- Компонент из очереди вне `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` отвечает «not found», не называя скрытую очередь, как это делают issue-тулы.
- `clear_lead` добавлен сверх PR, раз механизм подтверждён.
- Модули названы `component.py` / `component_write.py` по образцу `board.py`, а не `component_read.py` из PR.

```
feat: queue component tools (#30)

Finishes PR #30 on top of the current main: queue_get_components,
component_get, component_create, component_update, component_delete.

- Reads use GET v3/queues/{queue}/components and GET v3/components/{id}

  listing is not used - it pages through every component the organization has.
- component_update takes an optional version (the API answers 428 without
  one and 412, not 409, for a stale one - the funnel maps both onto
  conflict=), reads the component once when the caller gave no version or a
  queue restriction needs its queue, and refuses an empty update locally.
  clear_lead sends the {} that removes the lead.
- TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES / TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES apply through the
  component's queue; a component in a hidden queue is reported as not found.
- Component reads are not cached: their version is what the PATCH must send.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

## What changed against #30

- **Read side.** `queue_get_components(queue_id)` on the undocumented `GET v3/queues/{queue}/components` (the full objects of one queue, one request) replaces the org-wide `components_get_all`, which on a real organization walks 1002 components in 21 requests to find a queue's 13. `queue_get_metadata` with `expand=components` is untouched: it names components (id and name) for `issue_create` / `issue_update`; `queue_get_components` is what carries `lead`, `assignAuto` and the `version` an update needs.

- `TRACKER_LIMIT_QUEUES` / `TRACKER_READ_ONLY_QUEUES` apply through the component's queue. A component in a queue the allow-list hides is reported as not found rather than naming the queue, as issues are.
- `clear_lead` on `component_update`, sending the `{}` that removes the lead.
- Component reads are not cached under `TOOLS_CACHE_ENABLED`: their `version` is what the PATCH must send, and there is no omit-version escape as there is for issues.
- Internal: `ChecklistItemClearConflict` is now `FieldClearConflict`, shared with the component update; the `check_*_access` helpers share one `_check_scoped_queue`; `_request()` maps 412 onto `conflict=` next to 409.

## Verified on a live organization (2026-09-06)

| Endpoint | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET v3/queues/{key}/components` (undocumented) | full objects of that queue, no pagination |
| `GET v3/components/{id}` (undocumented) | full object; 404 for an unknown id |
| `GET v3/queues/{key}?expand=components` | references only: `id` as a string and `display` |
| `PATCH v3/components/{id}` without `version` | 428 |
| `PATCH` with a stale `version` | 412, not 409 |
| `PATCH` with an empty body | 200 and nothing changes; refused locally |
| `PATCH` `lead` | a login, a uid (number or string) or `{"id": ...}` all work; `{}` clears, `null` is ignored, `""` answers 422 |
| `DELETE v3/components/{id}` (undocumented) | 204, takes no `version`; a second delete answers 404 |

The full account is in AGENTS.md under *Queue components*.

- [x] Create, update, stale-version update and delete exercised on a live organization with a throwaway component, deleted afterwards
